title: Speaking and listening
intro: Spanish separates decir (to say the words) from hablar (to talk), contar (to tell a story) and platicar or charlar (to chat). English overloads say, tell and talk; Spanish does not.

ex.es: Le dieron la palabra al testigo.
ex.en: They gave the witness the floor.

entries.note: la oración is the grammatical term for a sentence, and also a prayer.
Masculine despite the -a. la lengua also means language, and the tongue.
contar con means to count on, to rely on.

ex.en: Could you explain it to me again?

entries.note: responder is the slightly more formal synonym. la respuesta is the answer.
el grito is a shout. dar un grito is to let out a yell.

ex.es: No me grites, te escucho bien.
ex.en: Don't shout at me, I can hear you.

entries.en: to be quiet, to stop talking
entries.note: ¡Cállate! is blunt — shut up. el silencio is silence.

entries.en: to call, to phone; to be called (llamarse)
entries.note: ¿Cómo te llamas? is literally what do you call yourself.
mandar or enviar un mensaje is to send a message.
Plural voces. en voz alta means out loud; en voz baja quietly.

ex.en: He has a very deep voice.

entries.note: hacer ruido is to make a noise; ruidoso is noisy.

ex.en: The neighbours make a lot of noise.

entries.note: Hearing that happens to you, as against escuchar, which is deliberate. ¡Oye! is hey.

ex.es: No te oigo, habla más fuerte.
ex.en: I can't hear you, speak louder.

entries.note: el sustantivo is a noun, el adjetivo an adjective, el acento the accent mark.
¿Qué significa esta palabra? is how to ask what a word means. querer decir does the same job.

ex.en: Will you translate this sentence for me?

entries.note: contar un chiste is to tell a joke. la broma is a prank.

ex.en: He told us a terrible joke.

entries.note: Singular for one item, plural las noticias for the news broadcast.

ex.es: Vemos las noticias a las nueve.
ex.en: We watch the news at nine.

entries.en: to lie, to tell a lie
entries.note: la mentira is a lie; la verdad the truth.
